dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Lembre-se: se a reta está dividida em partes de 1/4, onde fica o número 1 inteiro em termos de quartos?
Tente contar os intervalos de 1/4 começando do zero. Onde você pararia ao contar seis desses intervalos?
O número 1 na reta equivale a 4/4. Se você precisa de 6/4, conte dois intervalos além do número 1.
Você está quase lá! O ponto deve ficar exatamente na metade do caminho entre o 1 e o 2. Tente marcar o ponto ali.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: A fraction has two numbers. Which number tells how many parts are being considered?
Find the number above the fraction bar and enter it in the top field.
Look at the first number in the fraction written in the problem.
Type the top number of 6/4 into f1.
Which number tells how many equal parts make one whole?
Find the number below the fraction bar and enter it in the bottom field.
Look at the second number in the fraction written in the problem.
Type the bottom number of 6/4 into f2.
Compare the number of parts with the number of parts needed to make one whole.
Use the denominator to identify how many fourths make one whole.
The fraction contains more than one group of four equal parts, so look beyond the starting point.
Place the point on the whole-number mark reached after one complete group of fourths.
An improper fraction can be rewritten as whole groups plus the remaining fractional parts.
Divide the numerator by the denominator. Use the quotient for the whole-number part and the remainder for the new numerator.
One group of four fits into six, leaving two parts, while the denominator stays the same.
Enter the quotient as the whole number, the remainder as the fractional numerator, and keep the denominator 4.
The denominator tells you how many equal intervals make one unit on the number line.
Divide each unit into four equal intervals, then count the numerator's number of intervals from zero.
After four fourths you reach one whole; continue counting two more fourth-size intervals.
Starting at zero, count six equal intervals and click the matching position to the right of 1.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and its position on the number line represent the same quantity.
Review the top and bottom fraction fields, the converted mixed number, and the marked point.
Make sure the point is two fourth-size intervals to the right of 1.
When every field and the number-line point are correct, press the Done button once.

nodes.description: Click Convert to rewrite 6/4 as a mixed number.

hints.message: An improper fraction can be rewritten as whole groups plus the remaining fractional parts.
Divide the numerator by the denominator. Use the quotient for the whole-number part and the remainder for the new numerator.
One group of four fits into six, leaving two parts, while the denominator stays the same.
Enter the quotient as the whole number, the remainder as the fractional numerator, and keep the denominator 4.

misconceptions.description: O aluno inverte a lógica da conversão de fração imprópria para número misto
misconceptions.feedback: You reversed the roles of the numbers. Divide 6 by 4: the quotient is the whole part, the remainder is the numerator, and 4 remains the denominator.

nodes.description: Mark the point for 6/4 on the number line from 0 to 2.

hints.message: The denominator tells you how many equal intervals make one unit on the number line.
Divide each unit into four equal intervals, then count the numerator's number of intervals from zero.
After four fourths you reach one whole; continue counting two more fourth-size intervals.
Starting at zero, count six equal intervals and click the matching position to the right of 1.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ignora a escala fracionária e marca o ponto no número inteiro correspondente ao numerador
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the numerator as a whole-number location. The number line uses fourths, so six fourth-size intervals land between 1 and 2.

misconceptions.description: O aluno conta as marcas (ticks) em vez dos intervalos entre elas
misconceptions.feedback: You counted one extra interval. Count the spaces between marks from zero and stop after six fourth-size intervals.

misconceptions.description: O aluno ancora o valor na metade da reta (1/2) por ser uma referência familiar
misconceptions.feedback: You marked the halfway reference instead of the value of the fraction. Because 6/4 is greater than 1, the point belongs to the right of 1.

nodes.description: Click Done after entering the fraction and marking 6/4 on the number line.
nodes.instruction: Click Done after entering the fraction and marking 6/4 on the number line.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that the fraction and its position on the number line represent the same quantity.
Review the top and bottom fraction fields, the converted mixed number, and the marked point.
Make sure the point is two fourth-size intervals to the right of 1.
When every field and the number-line point are correct, press the Done button once.
